nhl-flyers.claim: In 2016–17 the Flyers won ten straight games in November and December but were eliminated from playoff contention, becoming the first team to miss the playoffs after a winning streak of ten or more games.
nhl-flyers.proof: In the 2016–17 season, the Flyers won ten straight games during the months of November and December. However, they fell out of the playoff picture after that streak ended, struggling in the standings and letting other teams get ahead of them. They were eliminated from playoff contention during the last two weeks of the regular season, becoming the first team to miss the playoffs after having a winning streak of ten or more games in the process.

nhl-goldenknights.text: Fun fact. The Golden Knights were not the first choice: the owner hoped to call the team the Black Knights, but dropped the plan after resistance from federal officials!
nhl-goldenknights.claim: The Vegas team's founder had hoped to name it the Black Knights but dropped that plan after encountering resistance from federal officials; the team became the Golden Knights.
nhl-goldenknights.proof: Foley had hoped to name his team the Black Knights, but dropped that plan after encountering resistance from federal officials.

nhl-goldenknights.text: Fun fact. In their first season the Golden Knights reached the Stanley Cup Final, but the Washington Capitals defeated them in five games!
nhl-goldenknights.claim: In their inaugural season the Golden Knights reached the Stanley Cup Final and were defeated there by the Washington Capitals in five games.
nhl-goldenknights.proof: On May 20, Vegas defeated the Winnipeg Jets to win the conference finals in five games, becoming the third NHL team to advance to the Stanley Cup Final in its inaugural season ... The Golden Knights were defeated in the Stanley Cup Final by the Washington Capitals in five games

nhl-goldenknights.text: Fun fact. The Golden Knights suffered their first-ever first-round elimination, losing to the Sharks in seven games after leading the series 3 games to 1!
nhl-goldenknights.claim: The Golden Knights suffered their first-ever first-round elimination, losing to the San Jose Sharks in seven games after leading the series 3 games to 1.
nhl-goldenknights.proof: They ultimately suffered their first-ever first-round elimination, losing to the San Jose Sharks in seven games after leading the series 3 games to 1.

nhl-goldenknights.text: Fun fact. Vegas' playoff run again ended one round short of the Stanley Cup Final when the Golden Knights were upset by Montreal in six games!
nhl-goldenknights.claim: The Golden Knights' 2020–21 playoff run ended one round short of the Stanley Cup Final when they were upset by the Montreal Canadiens in six games in the semifinals.
nhl-goldenknights.proof: Vegas' playoff run would again end one round short of the Stanley Cup Final, as the Golden Knights were then upset by the Montreal Canadiens in six games in the Stanley Cup semifinals.

nhl-goldenknights.text: Fun fact. In the 2024 Winter Classic the Golden Knights lost 3–0 to Seattle, becoming the first team to be shut out in the Winter Classic!
nhl-goldenknights.claim: In the 2024 Winter Classic the Golden Knights lost 3–0 to Seattle and became the first team to be shut out in the Winter Classic.
nhl-goldenknights.proof: January also saw the Golden Knights compete in the 2024 Winter Classic on New Year's Day, facing off against Seattle at T-Mobile Park in their second outdoor game; Vegas ultimately lost 3–0, becoming the first team to be shut out in the Winter Classic.

nhl-hurricanes.text: Fun fact. The Carolina Hurricanes looked poised to pick up where they left off in 2002–03, but a 10-loss January left them dead last in the league!
nhl-hurricanes.claim: The Hurricanes looked poised to pick up where they left off in 2002–03 but never recovered from a 10-loss January and finished dead last in the league with 61 points.
nhl-hurricanes.proof: The Hurricanes looked poised to pick up where they left off in the 2002–03, but never recovered from a 10-loss January and finished dead last in the league with 61 points

nhl-hurricanes.text: Fun fact. After winning the Cup, the Carolina Hurricanes missed the playoffs in 2006–07 and 2007–08, only the second club in NHL history to miss two seasons running after a Cup triumph!
nhl-hurricanes.claim: The Hurricanes failed to qualify for the playoffs in 2006–07 and 2007–08, only the second club in NHL history to miss two seasons running after a Stanley Cup triumph.
nhl-hurricanes.proof: Losing four players to free agency in the off-season and 222-man games to injury during the 2006–07, the team struggled throughout the regular season, and once eliminated in the last game, the Hurricanes finished third in the Southeast and 11th overall in the Eastern Conference. This finish made them the first champions since the 1938–39 Chicago Black Hawks to have failed to qualify for the playoffs both the seasons before and after their championship season ... In the 2007–08, Carolina again missed out as Washington Capitals stormed back to take the division title on the last day of the season, leaving the Hurricanes second in the division and ninth overall in the conference, and making the Hurricanes only the second club in NHL history to miss the playoffs for two seasons running after a Stanley Cup triumph.

nhl-hurricanes.text: Fun fact. The Carolina Hurricanes missed the playoffs eight seasons in a row, finishing last in the Metropolitan Division in 2014–15 along the way!
nhl-hurricanes.claim: The Hurricanes missed the playoffs for eight consecutive seasons, including finishing last in the Metropolitan Division in 2014–15 and seventh in 2016–17.
nhl-hurricanes.proof: During the 2014–15 season, the team finished last in the Metropolitan Division and would miss the playoffs for the sixth consecutive season ... Things did not improve in the 2016–17 season. The Hurricanes finished seventh in the division, missing the playoffs for the eighth consecutive season.

nhl-hurricanes.text: Fun fact. The Carolina Hurricanes won their division in 2022–23, then got swept 0–4 by Florida in the conference finals!
nhl-hurricanes.claim: After winning their division in 2022–23, the Hurricanes were swept 0–4 by the Florida Panthers in the conference finals.

nhl-hurricanes.text: Fun fact. In their first Stanley Cup Final, the Carolina Hurricanes stunned Detroit in game one, then lost the next four games!
nhl-hurricanes.claim: In their first Stanley Cup Final the Hurricanes won game one in overtime over the Red Wings, then Detroit won the next four games.
nhl-hurricanes.proof: Carolina's Martin Gélinas would score to send the franchise to their first Stanley Cup Final appearance ... In the Stanley Cup Final, Carolina would face the Detroit Red Wings, thought to be the prohibitive favorite all year. Though the Hurricanes stunned the Wings in game one when Ron Francis scored in the first minute of overtime, Detroit stormed back to win the next four games.

nhl-islanders.text: Fun fact. In their first season the Islanders set an NHL record for most losses and worst overall record in a season!
nhl-islanders.claim: In their first season the expansion Islanders set an NHL record for most losses and worst overall record in a season.
nhl-islanders.proof: In the team's first season, young players such as Smith, Nystrom, and Henning (all of whom would be part of the Islanders dynasty of the early 1980s) were given chances to prove themselves in the NHL. The young and inexperienced expansion team, however, posted a record of 12–60–6, setting an NHL record for most losses and worst overall record in a season.

nhl-islanders.text: Fun fact. The 1988–89 Islanders won only seven of their first 27 games and finished tied with Quebec for the worst record in the league!
nhl-islanders.claim: In 1988–89 the Islanders won only seven of their first 27 games and finished with 61 points, tied with the Quebec Nordiques for the worst record in the league.
nhl-islanders.proof: The 1988–89 season saw the Islanders win only seven of their first 27 games. ... and the team finished with 61 points, tied with the Quebec Nordiques for the worst record in the league.

nhl-islanders.text: Fun fact. The Islanders barely made the 1994 playoffs, then got swept in a lopsided opening series by the first-place Rangers!
nhl-islanders.claim: The Islanders barely squeezed into the 1994 playoffs, then were swept in a lopsided opening series by the first-place Rangers, who went on to win the Cup.
nhl-islanders.proof: The Islanders barely squeezed past the Panthers to make the 1994 playoffs before being swept in a lopsided opening series by the first-place Rangers, who went on to win the Cup.

nhl-islanders.text: Fun fact. In the lockout-shortened 1994–95 season the Islanders missed the playoffs and finished ahead of only the third-year Ottawa Senators!
nhl-islanders.claim: In the lockout-shortened 1994–95 season the Islanders failed to qualify for the playoffs and finished ahead of only the third-year Ottawa Senators.
nhl-islanders.proof: In the lockout-shortened 1994–95 season, the Islanders not only failed to qualify for the playoffs, they finished ahead of only the third-year Ottawa Senators.

nhl-islanders.text: Fun fact. Rangers fans mockingly called the Islanders "fishsticks" over their new fisherman logo, and it was a disappointing year on the ice too: they finished in last place!
nhl-islanders.claim: After the Islanders unveiled a new fisherman logo, rival Rangers fans mockingly called them "fishsticks", and the same year the team finished in last place.
nhl-islanders.proof: The same year, the Islanders' attempt at updating their look resulted in the unveiling of a new team logo of a slicker-clad fisherman holding a hockey stick. Islanders fans disliked it, and rival Rangers' fans mockingly called the Islanders "fishsticks"—mocking how the logo resembled the Gorton's Fisherman. ... The year was a disappointment on the ice as well, as the Islanders finished in last place with a record of 22–50–10.

nhl-jets.text: Fun fact. In 12 years in Atlanta, the franchise that became the Winnipeg Jets made the playoffs once and never won a playoff game!
nhl-jets.claim: In their 12 years in Atlanta the Thrashers (now the Jets franchise) qualified for the playoffs once, in 2006–07, and never won a playoff game.
nhl-jets.proof: In the 12 years in Atlanta, the Thrashers qualified for the Stanley Cup playoffs once, during the 2006–07 season, and never won a playoff game.

nhl-jets.text: Fun fact. In 2015 the Winnipeg Jets clinched their first playoff spot since relocating, then were swept in four games by the Anaheim Ducks in the first round!
nhl-jets.claim: On April 9, 2015 the Jets clinched their first playoff appearance since relocating to Winnipeg, then were swept in four games by the top-seeded Ducks in the first round.
nhl-jets.proof: On April 9, 2015, the Jets clinched their first Stanley Cup playoff appearance since relocating to Winnipeg ... they played the top-seeded Anaheim Ducks in the first round. In the first playoff series that involved a team from Winnipeg since the 1996 playoffs, the Ducks swept the Jets in four games.

nhl-jets.text: Fun fact. The season after their first playoff run, the Winnipeg Jets finished 25th overall, then won the second overall pick through the draft lottery!
nhl-jets.claim: The season after their first playoff run the Jets finished 25th overall, well out of the playoffs, yet won the second overall pick in the 2016 draft lottery despite the sixth-worst record.
nhl-jets.proof: The season following their first playoff run was a disappointment, as the Jets finished 25th overall, well out of the playoffs ... Despite finishing with the sixth-worst record in the league, the Jets managed to win the second overall pick in the 2016 NHL entry draft through the draft lottery

nhl-jets.text: Fun fact. In 2018 the Winnipeg Jets won game 1 of the conference finals against Vegas 4–2, then lost the next four games!
nhl-jets.claim: In the 2018 conference finals the Jets won game 1 against the Golden Knights 4–2, then Vegas won the following four games.
nhl-jets.proof: On April 11, 2018, the Jets won the first playoff game in the history of the Atlanta/Winnipeg franchise when they defeated the Minnesota Wild 3–2 ... Facing the Vegas Golden Knights in the conference finals, the Jets defeated the Golden Knights in the first game of the series 4–2. However, the Jets went on to lose the conference finals, with the Golden Knights defeating the Jets in the following four games in the series.

nhl-jets.text: Fun fact. In 2024–25 the Winnipeg Jets won their first Presidents Trophy, then lost to Dallas in six games in the second round!
nhl-jets.claim: In 2024–25 the Jets won their first Presidents Trophy and division championship, beat St. Louis in seven games, then lost to the Dallas Stars in six games in the second round.
nhl-jets.proof: During the 2024–25 season, the Jets won their first Presidents Trophy and their division championship for most wins (56), most points (116). They would then win against the St. Louis Blues in the first round in seven games  before eventually losing to the Dallas Stars in six games.

nhl-kings.text: Fun fact. The Los Angeles Kings won game 1 of the 1993 Stanley Cup Final and led game 2 late, but never recovered and lost to Montreal!
nhl-kings.claim: In the 1993 Final the Kings won game 1 and led game 2 2–1 late, but never recovered: they dropped the next two games in overtime and lost game 5, giving Montreal its 24th Cup.
nhl-kings.proof: In the 1993 Stanley Cup Final, the Kings faced the Montreal Canadiens. They won the first game 4–1, but late in game 2, with the Kings leading by a score of 2–1, Canadiens coach Jacques Demers requested a measurement of Kings defenseman Marty McSorley's stick blade ... and the Kings never recovered. They dropped the next two games in overtime, and lost game 5, 4–1, giving the Canadiens their league-leading 24th Stanley Cup in franchise history.

nhl-kings.text: Fun fact. The Los Angeles Kings' 1995–96 alternate jersey was so unpopular with fans that it was scrapped after only one season!
nhl-kings.claim: The Kings' alternate jersey for 1995–96, the so-called "Burger King" jersey, was unpopular with fans and was scrapped after one season.
nhl-kings.proof: The Kings briefly reintroduced purple and gold to the color scheme upon unveiling an alternate jersey for the 1995–96 season ... The so-called "Burger King" jersey proved to be unpopular with fans, and was scrapped after only one season.

nhl-kings.text: Fun fact. The Los Angeles Kings entered 2014–15 as early favorites to retain their title, then missed the playoffs, only the fourth team to do so as defending winners since 1967!
nhl-kings.claim: The Kings, favorites to retain their title in 2014–15, missed the postseason, only the fourth defending Cup champion to do so since the 1967 expansion.
nhl-kings.proof: Having won two Stanley Cup championships in the last three years, the Kings entered the 2014–15 season as the early favorites to retain their title ... the Kings became the first defending Stanley Cup champion to miss the postseason since the 2006–07 Carolina Hurricanes and only the fourth overall since the 1967 NHL expansion season.

nhl-kings.text: Fun fact. The Los Angeles Kings began 2023–24 with an NHL-record road streak, then suddenly won just three of 17 games before the All-Star break!
nhl-kings.claim: In 2023–24 the Kings broke the NHL record for the longest unbeaten road streak to start a year, then won just three of their final 17 games before the All-Star break.
nhl-kings.proof: The 2023–24 season got off to a strong start, as the team began the season with an 11–0–0 record on the road, breaking the NHL record (previously held by the Buffalo Sabres) for the longest unbeaten road streak to start the year ... However, in January 2024, the Kings' season collapsed; despite making no major lineup or personnel changes, the Kings suddenly won just three of their final 17 games before the All-Star break.

nhl-kings.text: Fun fact. The Los Angeles Kings opened their first season in Long Beach because the Forum was unfinished, and the Forum's opener was a 2–0 shutout loss!
nhl-kings.claim: In 1967–68 the Kings opened at Long Beach Arena because the Forum was not complete; the Forum opened December 30, 1967 with the Kings shut out 2–0 by the Flyers.
nhl-kings.proof: Construction on Cooke's new arena, the Forum, was not yet complete when the 1967–68 season began, so the Kings opened their first season at the Long Beach Arena in the neighboring city of Long Beach on October 14, 1967, defeating another expansion team, the Philadelphia Flyers, 4–2. The "Fabulous Forum" finally opened its doors on December 30, 1967, with the Kings being shut out by the Flyers, 2–0.

nhl-kraken.text: Fun fact. The Seattle Kraken lost their first game and their first home game, then finished their inaugural season last in the Pacific Division!
nhl-kraken.claim: The Kraken lost their first regular season game (4–3 to Vegas) and first home game (4–2 to Vancouver), and finished their inaugural season in last place of the Pacific Division.
nhl-kraken.proof: The Kraken played their first regular season game the next day, a 4–3 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights ... The Kraken played their first home game at Climate Pledge Arena (formerly KeyArena) on October 23, a 4–2 loss to the division rival Vancouver Canucks ... The Kraken finished their inaugural season in last place of the Pacific Division

nhl-kraken.text: Fun fact. In 2023–24 the Seattle Kraken had a franchise-record nine-game win streak and still missed the playoffs!
nhl-kraken.claim: In 2023–24 the Kraken had a franchise record nine-game win streak yet missed the playoffs.
nhl-kraken.proof: In December and January, following an eight-game losing streak, goaltender Joey Daccord started in eight out of nine games of a franchise record nine-game win streak ... During the 2023–24 season, the team missed the playoffs, scoring only 217 goals and achieving only 81 points.

nhl-kraken.text: Fun fact. Before their first season, the Seattle Kraken's home preseason games were held in Spokane, Everett and Kent because their arena renovation was delayed!
nhl-kraken.claim: The Kraken's three home preseason games before 2021–22 were in Spokane, Everett and Kent due to delays in the renovation of Climate Pledge Arena.
nhl-kraken.proof: The Kraken's three home preseason games prior to the 2021–22 season were held at Spokane Arena in Spokane, Angel of the Winds Arena in Everett, and the accesso ShoWare Center in Kent: arenas home to Western Hockey League (WHL) teams, in an event known as the 3-Rink Rush, due to delays in the renovation of Climate Pledge Arena.

nhl-kraken.text: Fun fact. In 2022–23 the Seattle Kraken won their first playoff series by upsetting the Avalanche in seven games, then lost to Dallas in the second round!
nhl-kraken.claim: In 2022–23 the Kraken upset the Avalanche in seven games, the first expansion team to win its first playoff series over the defending champion, then lost to the Stars in the second round.
nhl-kraken.proof: During the 2022–23 season, the team achieved a record of 46–28–8 and 100 points, securing fourth place in the Pacific Division ... They upset the Avalanche in seven games, becoming the first expansion team to win their first playoff series over the defending Stanley Cup champion. However, they lost to the Dallas Stars in the second round

nhl-kraken.text: Fun fact. The Seattle Kraken's 2024 Winter Classic uniform leaked four days before its unveiling when NBA Utah Jazz players walked into their arena wearing it!
nhl-kraken.claim: The Kraken's 2024 Winter Classic uniform, unveiled November 22, 2023, leaked four days earlier when Utah Jazz players walked into their home arena wearing it.
nhl-kraken.proof: For the 2024 NHL Winter Classic, the Kraken wore a uniform inspired by the Seattle Metropolitans ... The uniform was officially unveiled on November 22, 2023, but was leaked four days earlier when players from the National Basketball Association's Utah Jazz walked into their home arena wearing it.

nhl-lightning.text: Fun fact. The Tampa Bay Lightning rose to the top of their division within a month of their first season, then finished in last place!
nhl-lightning.claim: In their first season the Lightning rose to the top of the Norris Division within a month, but finished in last place.
nhl-lightning.proof: The Lightning played their first regular season game on October 7, 1992, in Tampa's Expo Hall at the Florida State Fairgrounds ... The team rose to the top of the Campbell Conference's Norris Division within a month, behind Kontos' initial torrid scoring pace and a breakout season by forward Brian Bradley. However, the team finished in last place

nhl-lightning.text: Fun fact. After a third straight Stanley Cup Final in 2022, the Tampa Bay Lightning lost in the first round of the playoffs in each of the next four seasons, 2022–23 through 2025–26!
nhl-lightning.claim: After clinching a third straight Final berth in 2022, the Lightning lost in the first round in 2022–23, 2023–24, 2024–25 and 2025–26.
nhl-lightning.proof: On June 11, the Lightning clinched their third straight Stanley Cup Final berth defeating the New York Rangers in game six of the conference finals ... In the 2022–23 season, the Lightning finished in third place in the Atlantic Division and sixth in the Eastern Conference, and once again played the Toronto Maple Leafs in the first round of the 2023 playoffs. However, the Maple Leafs eliminated the Lightning 4–2. In the 2023–24 season, the Lightning finished in fourth place in the Atlantic Division, and qualified for the 2024 playoffs as the first wild card, but were eliminated by their in–state rivals, the Florida Panthers, in five games in the first round ... In the 2024–25 season, they played the Florida Panthers in the first round of the playoffs and lost in five games. The 2025–26 season ended with another first round playoff loss, this time against the Montreal Canadiens in seven games.

nhl-lightning.text: Fun fact. The Tampa Bay Lightning lost 54 games in 1999–2000 and 52 in 2000–01, becoming the first NHL team to post four straight 50-loss seasons!
nhl-lightning.claim: The Lightning lost 54 games in 1999–2000 and 52 in 2000–01, becoming the first team in NHL history to post four straight 50-loss seasons.
nhl-lightning.proof: the Lightning lost 54 games in 1999–2000 and 52 in 2000–01, becoming the first team in NHL history to post four straight 50-loss seasons.

nhl-lightning.text: Fun fact. In 2018–19 the Tampa Bay Lightning won the Presidents' Trophy, then became the first winner swept in the first round of the playoffs, by eighth-seeded Columbus!
nhl-lightning.claim: In 2018–19 the Lightning clinched the Presidents' Trophy, then were swept in four games in the 2019 first round by the eighth seeded Blue Jackets, the first Presidents' Trophy winner swept in the first round.
nhl-lightning.proof: During the 2018–19 season, the Lightning clinched their first Presidents' Trophy ... However, in the first round of the 2019 playoffs, they were swept in four games by the eighth seeded Columbus Blue Jackets, becoming the first Presidents' Trophy winner to be swept in the first round of the playoffs.

nhl-lightning.text: Fun fact. In 2014–15 the Tampa Bay Lightning beat three Original Six teams in the first three rounds, then lost the Stanley Cup Final to Chicago in six games!
nhl-lightning.claim: In 2014–15 the Lightning defeated three Original Six teams in the first three rounds, then lost the Stanley Cup Final to the Blackhawks in six games.
nhl-lightning.proof: Prior to the 2014–15 season, the Lightning drafted Brayden Point at 79th overall ... In the playoffs, they defeated the Detroit Red Wings in the first round, the Montreal Canadiens in the second round, and the New York Rangers in the Eastern Conference final ... They also became the first team to successfully defeat three Original Six teams in the first three rounds ... However, they lost the series in six games.

nhl-mapleleafs.text: Fun fact. The Maple Leafs franchise, then the Arenas, sold stars to pay legal bills in 1918–19 and won just five games, still its worst winning percentage!
nhl-mapleleafs.claim: In 1918–19 legal bills forced the Arenas (the Maple Leafs franchise) to sell stars, resulting in a five-win season with a .278 winning percentage, the worst in franchise history.
nhl-mapleleafs.proof: Mounting legal bills from the dispute forced the Arenas to sell some of their stars, resulting in a horrendous five-win season in 1918–19. ... The Arenas' .278 winning percentage that season remains the worst in franchise history.

nhl-mapleleafs.text: Fun fact. In 1952–53 the Maple Leafs failed to make the playoffs for the first time since 1945–46!
nhl-mapleleafs.claim: In the 1952–53 season the Maple Leafs failed to make the postseason for the first time since the 1945–46 playoffs.
nhl-mapleleafs.proof: With the conclusion of the 1952–53 regular season, the Leafs failed to make it to the postseason for the first time since the 1945–46 playoffs.

nhl-mapleleafs.text: Fun fact. In 1972–73 the Maple Leafs, undermanned and demoralized after losing key players to the new WHA, finished with the fourth-worst record in the league!
nhl-mapleleafs.claim: In 1972–73 the Maple Leafs, after losing key players to the new WHA, finished with the fourth-worst record in the league.
nhl-mapleleafs.proof: By the end of 1971, the World Hockey Association (WHA) began operations as a direct competitor to the NHL. Believing the WHA would not be able to compete against the NHL, Ballard's attitude caused the Maple Leafs to lose key players, including Parent to the upstart league. Undermanned and demoralized, the Leafs finished with the fourth-worst record for the 1972–73 season.

nhl-mapleleafs.text: Fun fact. In the 2013 playoffs the Maple Leafs blew a 4–1 third-period lead to the Bruins and lost 5–4 in overtime!
nhl-mapleleafs.claim: In the 2013 Stanley Cup playoffs the Bruins rallied from a 4–1 third-period deficit to beat the Maple Leafs 5–4 in overtime and advance.
nhl-mapleleafs.proof: The rivalry has since been renewed from the 2013 Stanley Cup playoffs which saw the Bruins rally from a 4–1 third-period deficit to defeat the Maple Leafs in overtime, 5–4, and advance to the second round.

nhl-mapleleafs.text: Fun fact. In 2025–26 the Maple Leafs finished last in the Atlantic Division, missing the playoffs for the first time since 2015–16!
nhl-mapleleafs.claim: In 2025–26 the Maple Leafs finished last in the Atlantic Division and missed the playoffs for the first time since 2015–16.
nhl-mapleleafs.proof: The team would end up finishing the 2025–26 season with a 32–36–14 record with 78 points, finishing last in the Atlantic Division, and missing the playoffs for the first time since the 2015–16 season.

nhl-oilers.text: Fun fact. In 1992–93 the Oilers missed the playoffs for the first time as an NHL team, and didn't return for four years!
nhl-oilers.claim: In 1992–93 the Oilers missed the playoffs for the first time as an NHL team and did not return to the postseason for four years.
nhl-oilers.proof: In 1992–93, they missed the playoffs for the first time as an NHL team. They did not return to the postseason for four years, despite the emergence of young centremen Doug Weight and Jason Arnott.

nhl-oilers.text: Fun fact. After coming up short in the 2006 Stanley Cup Final, the Oilers missed the playoffs for the next 10 straight seasons!
nhl-oilers.claim: After coming up short in the 2006 Stanley Cup Final, the Oilers missed the playoffs for the subsequent 10 seasons.
nhl-oilers.proof: The Oilers struggled after coming up short in the 2006 Stanley Cup Final, missing the playoffs for the subsequent 10 seasons.

nhl-oilers.text: Fun fact. In 1981–82 the Oilers finished second overall, then were upset by the Kings after blowing a 5–0 lead in game 3 — the Miracle on Manchester!
nhl-oilers.claim: In 1981–82 the Oilers finished second overall and were upset by the Kings in five games; in game 3 they took a 5–0 lead into the third period but lost 6–5 in overtime (the Miracle on Manchester).
nhl-oilers.proof: The Oilers improved in 1981–82, finishing second overall. ... They were upset by the Los Angeles Kings in a five-game series. In game 3 of this series, the Miracle on Manchester, the Oilers took a 5–0 lead into the third period, only to lose 6–5 in overtime).

nhl-oilers.text: Fun fact. In 2014–15 the Oilers earned only 62 points, one of their worst seasons as an NHL team!
nhl-oilers.claim: In 2014–15 the Oilers earned only 62 points in one of their worst seasons as an NHL team.
nhl-oilers.proof: Off-season moves failed to help the Oilers in the 2014–15 season, as the team earned only 62 points in one of their worst seasons as an NHL team.

nhl-oilers.text: Fun fact. In 1988–89 the Oilers led the Kings 3–1 in the first round, then lost game 7 6–3 in Los Angeles — their first first-round exit since 1982!
nhl-oilers.claim: In the 1988–89 first-round playoffs, the Oilers took a 3–1 series lead over the Los Angeles Kings but lost game 7 6–3 in Los Angeles, their first first-round elimination since 1982.
nhl-oilers.proof: The loss of Gretzky had an immediate impact in 1988–89 ... the Oilers' first-round playoff opponent was Gretzky's Los Angeles Kings. Edmonton took a commanding 3–1 series lead, but Gretzky and the Kings fought back to win the series, winning game 7 6–3 in Los Angeles. It was the first time since 1982 that the Oilers had been eliminated from the playoffs in the first round.

nhl-panthers.text: Fun fact. In 1997–98 the Panthers went through a 15-game winless streak on the way to the worst record in franchise history!
nhl-panthers.claim: In 1997–98 the Panthers posted a franchise-worst 24–43–15 record, including a 15-game winless streak.
nhl-panthers.proof: The team would plummet in the 1997–98 season. ... The change did not aid matters, as Florida posted a franchise-worst 24–43–15 record, including a 15-game winless streak.

nhl-panthers.text: Fun fact. In 2008–09 the Panthers had their second-highest finish ever with 93 points, yet missed the playoffs for an eighth-straight season, the then-longest streak in the NHL!
nhl-panthers.claim: In 2008–09 the Panthers earned 93 points, their second-highest finish in franchise history, yet missed the playoffs for an eighth-straight season, the then-longest streak in the NHL.
nhl-panthers.proof: The Panthers finished the 2008–09 season with a strong 41–30–11 record and 93 points, their second-highest finish in franchise history. Despite this, however, the Panthers missed the playoffs for an eighth-straight season, the then-longest streak in the NHL.

nhl-panthers.text: Fun fact. In 2012–13 the Panthers followed their first-ever division title with the worst record in the League!
nhl-panthers.claim: After winning the first division title in franchise history (April 2012), the Panthers had the worst record in the League in the lockout-shortened 2012–13 season.
nhl-panthers.proof: The Panthers won the first-ever division title in franchise history with a 4–1 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes on April 7, 2012. ... In the lockout-shortened 2012–13 season, the Panthers had an abysmal season. Unable to regain their form from last season, the Panthers suffered key injuries and fell back down into the basement with the worst record in the League.

nhl-panthers.text: Fun fact. In 2017–18 the Panthers earned 96 points, tying the NHL record for most points by a team to miss the postseason, ending one point short of a playoff berth!
nhl-panthers.claim: In 2017–18 the Panthers ended one point short of a playoff berth with 96 regular season points, tying the league record for the most regular season points to miss the postseason.
